newsitem.title: USA: Mich. Gov will veto road fund plan if no reforms.
newsitem.headline: Mich. Gov will veto road fund plan if no reforms.

text.p: Michigan Gov. John Engler will veto a $69 million appropriation from the state's "rainy day" fund for current road repairs if lawmakers fail to adopt his proposed transportation package, a spokesman said Thursday.

Lawmakers have adopted about half of Engler's proposals, which include the state assuming control of major local roads, increasing fees on truckers and streamlining insurance packages for construction projects, John Truscott said.
But Engler will reject the appropriation if his other plans are not adopted and still has not committed to it even if the rest are approved, Truscott said.
Michigan senators and representatives have recommended the appropriation, which would be a first-time dip into the budget stabilization fund for transportation purposes.
The transportation appropriation would take interest, but not principal, from the fund, which is projected to have from $1.2 billion to $1.3 billion by the end of fiscal 1998.
Because the two versions of the appropriation differed slightly, it remains in the Senate for consideration and has not yet been forwarded to Engler.
Engler hopes to have work on the transportation plans completed by the July 4 holiday weekend, but it may take until mid-July to resolve the issues, Truscott said.
